name: repo-fit
description: Give your project a memory: a session briefing, one list of everything open, safe automatic saves and one rulebook for Claude Code and Codex. Works on new and existing projects.
author: Jimmy Sadek

releases.why: repo-fit can now organize your folder: it shows the folder before and after, asks once, and keeps it organized. Nothing is deleted, and one command undoes it.
releases.briefing: New: repo-fit can organize your folder. Ask your assistant to run /repo-fit to see the plan. Nothing changes without your yes.
news: A map of your folder (MAP.md) and an index page per folder, so you and your assistant find any note in two steps.
Organize with one yes: loose files go into folders, old folders and exact copies go to an archive, and the screen shows before, after and why first. Nothing is deleted; one command undoes it.
Before any change, Git saves a snapshot of your folder, so you can always go back. A folder without Git gets Git started first.
New things go in inbox/ and are filed by the rules you approved, when a session starts.
The briefing names real problems in one short line each and stays quiet otherwise. Running /repo-fit again starts with a checkup.
Open tasks from all your notes are listed in one place, in MAP.md.

releases.why: Setup now asks you once instead of a dozen times, and the shared rules in AGENTS.md shrink to 293 words that never override yours.
news: The shared rules in AGENTS.md shrink from 774 to 293 words. They go after your own rules and say yours win where they overlap. No more rules about branches, when to commit, or board columns.
The briefing no longer says "never commit on main". Without a board, it shows your last three commits instead of an error.
A long list of unlinked notes in the briefing becomes a count, with one command that lists them.
You turn the start-of-session briefing on yourself with one line, because Claude Code does not let an assistant change how sessions start.

A reminder at the end of each reply: when files changed but nothing was written down, the assistant is asked once whether anything is worth keeping. It never pushes you to save; your rules decide that. Turn it on with the same one line as the briefing.

steps.D-01: The shared rules block is now 293 words, goes after your rules, and your rules win where they overlap. It no longer needs a table board or sets branch and commit rules.
